facts.shortSummary: Resting after their escape, the companions share memories of childhood, family, and home.
facts.longSummary: Seeker recalls his younger brother Frankar, a gifted rune-worker who secretly built a divination machine that killed white salamanders in different ways; after a violent storm, the machine lay shattered and Frankar had vanished, leaving one burned salamander. Delwath remembers baking rare sisila-fruit cakes for his elders as darkness spread beyond his homeland, and fears finding his home destroyed or transformed. Kenzo describes poverty and magical pollution in Chardon, his childhood visions, and his uneasy pull toward the city. Wellby remembers traveling the Green Sea with his family and a great-great-grandfather who taught that all places and times were one; for Wellby, the road remains home.

location.context: Breakfast camp south of Stormcaller Tower, outside the storm

facts.shortSummary: The party compares its unresolved mysteries and suspects connections among recent magical disturbances without settling on a cause.
facts.longSummary: Seeker reviews his journal: the storm comes from Hralgar, the tainted water was associated with a summoned demon, and Vola described Agata Dustmother as an unnaturally old human woman. The group questions whether Agata’s search for magical objects is connected to the demon summoners and how much to trust the storm’s answer that she seeks vengeance. They revisit the tower letters and the Occulta Ludum, learning that the Great Library preserves knowledge brought west after Drankor’s fall, but exhausted attempts to recall or translate more fail. Delwath describes escaping his imprisonment by something like cutting through it with shadow. The party wonders whether his return, Hralgar’s awakening, the missing eyes, and Chardonian treasure-seekers are connected, while agreeing to return to Alesh in Karawa.

facts.shortSummary: The mirror slowly recharges while the purple-lensed goggles reveal unusually fine details of nearby objects.
facts.longSummary: Delwath examines the mirror’s magic and finds it slowly absorbing energy away from a strong magical source; the party cannot yet tell whether its earlier vision showed only things the mirror had witnessed. They plan to walk south with their three heavily laden packhorses before making an early camp. Seeker checks the local ley lines, then tries the purple goggles: distant landscapes blur, but boots, the silver mirror, and a carved horn become sharply detailed. The mirror’s damaged wooden nameplate preserves an E and a U, suggesting Eudomes. The goggles reveal the horn’s wear and craftsmanship and confer an advantage on Arcana checks, though their full power remains undiscovered. The DM confirms the party has still not departed or recovered from exhaustion.

facts.shortSummary: Six starving, partly skeletal gnolls charge the exhausted travelers and are killed before the party camps for the night.
facts.longSummary: After only a few miles south, the party spots six gnolls moving west: an emaciated leader and five nearly skeletal followers. Unable to outrun them while exhausted, the companions prepare ranged attacks, and Wellby sends his axe beak clear. Initial shots mostly miss, but Wellby’s carefully aimed arrows wound the leader, Delwath uses Eldritch Blast and Hex, and Seeker’s Shatter destroys two followers. Kenzo’s Fist of Planar Power kills the leader; the survivors lash out and one bites Kenzo. Delwath’s Green-Flame Blade, Seeker’s Vicious Mockery, Wellby’s bow, and Kenzo’s final unarmed blows finish the rest. Inspection reveals little treasure and creatures sustained despite apparently consuming their own flesh. Their path could lead from Raven’s Hold, but their origin is unproven. The party moves away from the bodies and sleeps, beginning to recover from exhaustion.

mainEnemies.name: Five skeletal or nearly skeletal gnolls
mainEnemies.notes: All killed; their condition is described as undead-like self-consumption, not simple starvation.

combat.notes: All six enemies die. Kenzo takes a bite; the party remains together and camps afterward. Seeker destroys two with Shatter, Delwath kills one with Green-Flame Blade, Wellby kills one with an arrow, and Kenzo kills the leader and last follower.

facts.shortSummary: The party recovers during six days of travel and reaches a roadside camp half a day north of Karawa.
facts.longSummary: On April 17 the travelers resume their journey, and further rest clears their remaining exhaustion. The account advances roughly six days to April 23, when they camp beside the old trade road about half a day north of Karawa. Grassland has given way to dry, rocky scrub, and they expect to reach town the next day. Seeker maps the ley lines: one runs briefly near the road before veering away, while no visible line leads directly to the known node beneath Karawa’s Red Mesa.

location.context: Southward journey, April 17–23; final camp beside the old trade road

facts.shortSummary: Seeker identifies the mirror, and Delwath uses the ivory scroll cap to reveal a disturbing scene of its creation.
facts.longSummary: Further attempts to interpret the Occulta Ludum or remember the mirror’s earlier viewpoint fail. During the journey Seeker has worked out the Goggles of Object Reading; he now uses their Identify ability on the recharged Mirror of the Past. It reveals true images from the history of something reflected in it, though order and context may be misleading. The party chooses the ivory cap found beside the summoning circle at Raven’s Hold, and Delwath asks how it was first made and last used. The mirror shows a dark workshop, rhythmic activity, ivory pieces being carved, and letters burning onto skin resembling human or dwarven flesh. A black-gloved hand lifts the assembled object, and a long-tailed, horned creature becomes visible before the image fades. It differs from the creature they fought; the scene feels old, but its place, date, and maker remain unidentified.

facts.shortSummary: The vision prompts a discussion of planar connections, demonic bargains, and possible sources of the spreading corruption.
facts.longSummary: Delwath’s knowledge connects the use of flesh, fire, and blood with necromancy and magic binding the material world to human divine realms such as the Abyss and Nine Hells. The party discusses nearby and distant planes, ley lines as intersections with the Plane of Magic, and Kenzo’s limited ability to reach toward the Plane of Consciousness. Seeker wonders whether a similar direct manipulation could replace rune-work. Stories of bargains for power, corruption spilling through breaches, and wizards summoning servants offer possible explanations, but the group distinguishes folklore and speculation from evidence. The DM also notes that gnoll rampages have historical precedents. After a table break, the players briefly imagine a future flying stronghold before play advances to the next morning.

items.notes: The vision and the cumbersome mirror remain central to the discussion.

facts.shortSummary: Returning to a ruined Karawa, the party learns that the centaurs broke a gnoll siege of the temple.
facts.longSummary: The next morning the party walks the remaining miles to Karawa, where about a third of the town is ruined, the palms are gone, the oasis basin is cracked, and nine large graves stand on a rise. Havdar and a centaur patrol recognize them and escort them toward the temple; Ikram’s caravanserai and Delwath’s apartment lie destroyed, but Seeker’s fortifications have held. Candrosa looks exhausted and shaken. He reports that fifty or more gnolls arrived a few days after the party left; some continued west while roughly thirty besieged the temple. Nearly forty centaurs broke the siege eight or nine days earlier and remained to help. Candrosa had not understood that the party sent them: Tharandros spoke only of a chance meeting, danger, and promised knowledge of dreams. Candrosa thanks the companions before Alesh insists they exchange news.

facts.shortSummary: Alesh reports southern gnoll movements and disturbing dreams, while Candrosa describes Shakun’s defenses gradually failing.
facts.longSummary: Alesh recounts passing ruined Bas Udda and watching quiet, unsettling Kharsan. Camping south of Kharsan beside the Kharja brought nightmares of red mist, choking, and bodies, which she tentatively connects to the old Red Death. Farther south her scouts followed fifteen or twenty gnolls, about half skeletal, southwest into the Garamjala; they turned back rather than enter without supplies. A large raven seemed to follow the gnolls, then leave and return, but its significance is unknown. Seeker animates the reported movements on a map while the party compares attacks and searches for other sources. Candrosa sketches Shakun’s former boundary and explains that its confusing paths and illusions diverted enemies. Pressed on when it failed, he describes a gradual weakening from early this year and admits that Shakun ceased speaking to him about some things, without revealing all his order’s secrets.

facts.shortSummary: Alesh describes an empty desert house and orc scouts, and Candrosa offers a troubling possible lead on Agata Dustmother.
facts.longSummary: Alesh describes an incongruous sandstone house on the desert’s edge, with a courtyard, water, goats, fed chickens, and ordinary household belongings, but no occupant. She thinks someone had tended it recently and suspects magical water, but took nothing and did not search its chest. She also saw two orcs scouting apart from any obvious larger force; their organization surprised her, and she avoided close pursuit. Asked about Agata Dustmother, Candrosa does not recognize that name but suggests the Old Woman of the Dusts, supposedly living about a day south of Bas Udda. He has never seen her. His story describes magic sought in desperation, paid for with something like a thumb that later appears in unsettling dreams. The party considers whether the names refer to the same person, without resolving the identity or connecting the house to her.
